properties.description: Two legs, on Anthony's word 2026-09-14 ("two legs and no more"). LEG 1, the served reply: ReaderLens carries each person's name; lens_line renders "who:ajs (Anthony Sligar)" for both the recorded and the askable lists, so the sentence that already rides get_skill, list_skills and loop_status gives the agent the join it needs against the git author it can see. No email or other identity signal is recorded; names are already in the public export. LEG 2, the orientation skill's reader step: with more than one background recorded, match the git author to a recorded name, offer it in one sentence ("assuming you are AJ — if not, tell me who you are and your background"), do not ask again that session, and attribute what is captured to the same person. A lint contract (READER_CONTRACT) keeps the clause stated. Pinned by the_lens_names_the_person_beside_the_id.rs (four tests) and three lint checks, each observed failing first. Deliberately not built: the seat does not record the reader; a stated assumption plus a name on every lens line keeps a wrong guess visible without session state.
properties.name: The lens line names each recorded person beside their id, and orientation offers the git-author match as an assumption when more than one reader is recorded
